task: Review this fictional headline and short poll story in about 70–120 words. Check the counted unit, population claim, and status of the result against the supplied exercise log. Explain what the numbers can support without inventing representative sampling or treating repeated entries as distinct residents.
input:
MOST RESIDENTS APPROVE NEW FENCE COLOUR

The town has decided to paint the fence blue. Of 86 residents who voted, 48 supported blue and 38 opposed it. The poll is therefore an official mandate from the community.

facts.text: The synthetic online-poll log contains 86 entries.
Forty-eight entries support blue and 38 oppose it.
The form allowed repeated submissions and did not establish unique respondents.
The packet does not establish the views of residents who did not submit an entry.
The informal poll is advisory and no fence-colour decision has been adopted.

forbidden_additions: Eighty-six entries equated with 86 distinct residents.
A population majority, representative sample, or official mandate.
An adopted decision or invented unique-voter count.
preserve: The supported majority among entries, not a claim about all residents.
Advisory feedback distinguished from a binding decision.
